short: Insights into the Distinct Lithiation/Sodiation of Porous Co
title: Insights into the Distinct Lithiation/Sodiation of Porous Cobalt Oxide by in Operando Synchrotron X-ray Techniques and Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Simulations

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Bulk cobalt oxide anodes fade fast: low electronic conductivity and large volume change on cycling. Make a porous cobalt oxide (PCO) to shorten ion diffusion paths and buffer volume change.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1a (HYP/need), n2 (DES/architecture), n3 (PRC/synthesis), n1 (HYP/gap), n9 (DES/method), n10 (PRC/stimulus), n11 (PRC/stimulus)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: As-prepared PCO is a two-phase Co3O4 + CoO mixture. PCO is mesoporous: hysteretic type IV isotherm, pores mostly 5-7 nm.
states.detail: Absorbed: n4 (STR/phase/identity), n5 (STR/microstructure/porosity), n12 (STR/phase/identity), n13 (STR/microstructure/porosity), n15 (STR/phase/fraction), n16 (STR/microstructure/porosity). Premises: Co K-edge: CoO white line ~7725 eV, Co3O4 pre-edge 7710 and white line 7730 eV; Co foil shoulder ~7713 eV

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Co3O4 is far less Na-active than Li-active (degree of oxidation ~36% vs ~91% at 2 ps). Na capacity fading stems from poor sodiation activity (minor conversion), not from volume change.
states.detail: Absorbed: n17 (PRP/value), n18 (MEC/identification), n22 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Nanoporous electrodes shorten diffusion lengths and buffer conversion volume change

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Li/PCO keeps ~840-870 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C (initial reversible ~870). Na/PCO fades from ~870 (1st discharge) to ~70 mAh/g after 40 cycles at 0.1 C

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: PCO is highly Li-active but poorly Na-active; its Na fading reflects low sodiation activity, not volume change

nodes.title: SEM, TEM, F1

nodes.solves: PCO is mesoporous: hysteretic type IV isotherm, pores mostly 5-7 nm
nodes.note: text: 10-20 nm nanoparticles seen only by TEM (Fig. S1, not in packet); sizes re-measured against the 500 nm bar (~148 px)

nodes.title: XRD:synchrotron, F1
nodes.head: Rietveld calculation with Co3O4 and CoO phases overlays the HEXRD pattern; difference curve nearly flat
nodes.solves: As-prepared PCO is a two-phase Co3O4 + CoO mixture
nodes.necessity_reason: n4 keeps shown support from o6 after removal.

nodes.title: XRD:SAXS, XRD:synchrotron, F3, F4
nodes.head: Li SAXS contours at low q bend to lower q during discharge (~6-11 h) and do not return on charge. Li SAXS: 0.02 V and 3 V curves drop below OCV at 0.01-0.1 A-1; hump grows at ~0.2-0.3 A-1.
nodes.solves: Li/PCO pore structure changes strongly on discharge and does not recover on charge
nodes.note: 1.07 V curve overlaps OCV, consistent with text (SEI before 1.07 V) small residual change is visible in F3d, consistent with the paper's 'much smaller' (not zero) change 19.2 deg peak also broadens and moves to ~19.0 deg while fading (not stated in text)
nodes.necessity_reason: n13, n16, n12, n15 keeps shown support from o18, o20, o21, a2 after removal.

nodes.title: XAS:EXAFS, XAS:XANES, F5
nodes.head: Li XANES: discharged spectra lose the white line (~0.97) and match the Co foil shape; charged spectra differ from OCV. Na XANES: discharged spectra keep a strong white line (~1.25 at ~7728 eV), unlike Co foil; charged lie between CoO and Co3O4.
nodes.solves: Lithiation to 0.01 V fully converts PCO to amorphous/metallic Co; oxide reflections vanish
nodes.necessity_reason: n12, n15 keeps shown support from o15, o20, a2, o16 after removal.

nodes.title: XAS:XANES, F5
nodes.head: XANES contours: Li white-line maximum vanishes at each discharge and returns on charge; Na maximum persists all cycles
nodes.solves: Lithiation to 0.01 V fully converts PCO to amorphous/metallic Co; oxide reflections vanish
nodes.note: F5a is at 0.2 C, F5c at 0.1 C (panel labels); caption says 0.2 C for c
nodes.necessity_reason: n12 keeps shown support from o15, o18, o21 after removal.

nodes.solves: PCO is mesoporous: hysteretic type IV isotherm, pores mostly 5-7 nm

nodes.solves: Sodiation reduces PCO only slightly: crystalline oxide largely retained, no metallic Co
nodes.note: charge must go to side reactions (e.g. SEI) if Na conversion is minor; packet text does not reconcile this
